speaker: system-architect
content: ADR for the hybrid decision is up for review. growth-coach, anything on the framing you want me to tighten before I publish?

speaker: growth-coach
content: One thing — the revenue-impact framing. I'd lead with the bounded-margin-leak number rather than the carry-cost number. The exec audience cares about margin risk; $90/month doesn't move anyone.

speaker: system-architect
content: Fair. I'll reorder. cost-analyst — did your modelling find a worst-case margin-leak dollar number for the 5-minute window?

speaker: cost-analyst
content: Yes. Assuming pricing volatility of 2% per 5-minute window in a normal market and our quote-acceptance rate of 14%, worst-case margin leak during a pricing outage is approximately $340 per minute of outage. Over a typical 18-minute outage, that's $6,100.

speaker: growth-coach
content: $6.1k per outage, three outages per quarter — call it $18k/quarter of bounded leak under hybrid. Compare event-bus: same outages but eventually-consistent means leak doesn't stop at 5 minutes, can extend through the recovery window. We had no upper bound estimate for event-bus leak.

speaker: system-architect
content: Right — that's the key story. Hybrid bounds the leak; event-bus doesn't. I'll lead the ADR with that frame.

speaker: cost-analyst
content: One more thing — under hybrid, the leak doesn't apply when pricing is healthy. Under event-bus, the staleness applies *always*, not just during outages. So event-bus has a permanent low-grade leak plus the outage spike.

speaker: growth-coach
content: That's an even sharper framing. Hybrid: leak only during outages. Event-bus: leak always. Lead with that.

speaker: system-architect
content: Done. ADR-007 will read: 'Hybrid transport chosen over event-bus to avoid permanent eventual-consistency margin leak; bounded leak only during pricing outages.' Three-week effort, $90/month carry, $18k/quarter worst-case bounded leak.

speaker: cost-analyst
content: Looks right. I'll add the model assumptions as an appendix so the next architect can re-run the numbers if volatility or acceptance rate moves.
